name: Xavier_B
review: I'm a solo traveler and found Cozumel very easy to navigate. I just rented a scooter and rode around the island. The east side is deserted and beautiful. Roatan was a bit harder to do alone as the taxis are expensive for one person. I ended up joining a group for a snorkeling trip. Costa Maya is impossible to enjoy alone without spending a lot of money on a taxi or a tour. The port area is fine but everything is priced for tourists. I'd recommend Cozumel for anyone who likes to explore independently.

name: Daniel R.
review: Roatan ended up being the highlight for us. We booked a small-group snorkeling trip and the water clarity was unreal compared to what we've seen elsewhere. The boat ride was short and smooth, and we had plenty of time in the water without feeling rushed. Costa Maya felt very manufactured in comparison-we walked through the port area and didn't feel compelled to go further, so we headed back early. Cozumel was somewhere in between; we grabbed a taxi downtown and wandered around, which was enjoyable but crowded. Overall, the itinerary felt a bit uneven, but Roatan alone made it worth it.

name: Liam O'Connor
review: I'm a big diver so Roatan was the main event for me. The reef there is in much better shape than Cozumel. We did a two-tank dive and saw a few reef sharks and a massive grouper. The boat pick-up was right near the pier, very efficient. In Cozumel, the current was quite strong the day we were there, so the drift dive was a bit faster than I like. For Costa Maya, I decided to just relax. I walked down to the Malecón in Mahahual and found a small spot with a bucket of beers for twenty bucks. It was a nice break from the ship's prices. If you're a diver, Roatan is a must, but Cozumel is still decent for the convenience.

name: Aisling O'Connor
review: We had a mixed experience with the port excursions. In Roatan, we booked a 'semi-sub' tour to see the reef. It was great for my elderly mother who can't snorkel. We saw turtles and rays through the windows. However, the tour started 30 minutes late and we were worried about our afternoon plans. In Costa Maya, we went to the beach at Mahahual. The seaweed was quite bad that day, which isn't anyone's fault, but it made swimming difficult. The local vendors are also very persistent, which got tiring after an hour. Cozumel was our favorite stop. We went to the Mayan Cacao Company. We learned how to make traditional chocolate and the samples were delicious. The facility was clean and the staff were very professional. I think the time spent in Cozumel was just right, but I would have traded some Costa Maya time for more time in Roatan.

name: Jin_Woo
review: In Cozumel, we did the chocolate and tequila tour. It was okay, a bit touristy, but the lunch was decent. Roatan was the best for nature. We did the monkey sanctuary and it was the highlight of the whole cruise for my daughter. Costa Maya was our least favorite stop. It felt very manufactured and expensive. $15 for a margarita in Mexico feels like a rip-off. We stayed for an hour and then went back to the ship to use the gym. The itinerary overall was good, but the ports are getting very crowded with the new mega-ships.

name: Hugo Martinez
review: Cozumel was the easiest port to explore on our own, and we spent most of the time just walking around and stopping at small shops near the waterfront. Roatan was more excursion-based for us, and we did a zipline and beach combination that was fun but slightly rushed. Costa Maya didn't offer much for us without an excursion, so we stayed within the port zone. It was clean and safe but didn't feel like we experienced the destination itself. I'd say Cozumel works best for casual exploring while Roatan is better for planned activities.

name: Sonia Gupta
review: Roatan's Mahogany Bay is convenient because the ship docks right at the beach, but it's very artificial. If you want the real Honduras, you have to leave the gated area. We took a taxi to the East End and the scenery was breathtaking. Cozumel was great for a relaxing day at the Money Bar; great food and easy water access. In Costa Maya, we did the Bacalar Lagoon excursion. It is a very long drive, nearly 90 minutes each way, but the 'Lake of Seven Colors' is real. The water is stunningly blue. Just be prepared for a lot of time on a bus.

name: Priya Nair
review: I appreciated the variety of ports but found the scheduling a bit tight. In Roatan, our excursion included a wildlife stop and beach time, but both felt shortened. Costa Maya required the most planning because everything is far from the port. We chose a beach club and enjoyed it, but transportation took time. Cozumel was the easiest to manage independently, which made it less stressful.

name: Talia Brooks
review: Costa Maya ended up being our most relaxed stop because we didn't plan anything and just stayed in the port area. Roatan was more structured with a short excursion that included beach time. Cozumel was very active but also overwhelming with crowds, so we didn't explore as much as we expected. Roatan stood out as the most enjoyable day overall.

name: M_Thompson_Adventures
review: We did the Amazing Race excursion in Cozumel and it was a blast! You have to solve clues and run around the downtown area. It's a great way to see the city and interact with locals, though you'll be exhausted by the end. Roatan was much more about nature. We visited the Iguana farm which was... interesting. There are hundreds of them everywhere! It's a bit weird but definitely unique. Costa Maya was a bit of a 'meh' day. We did the fly fishing excursion but didn't catch anything. The guide tried hard, but the fish just weren't biting that day. Still, it was nice to be out on the water away from the ship crowds.

name: WanderlustWendy
review: Costa Maya was beautiful. We went to Maya Chan and it was the most relaxing day of my life. They only take a few people, so it was quiet, and the food was amazing. In Cozumel, we did the Amazing Race excursion. It was a fun way to see the town and interact with locals, though we were running around so much we didn't really get to 'see' the sights. Roatan was a bit disappointing. We went to a beach club that was recommended, but it was so noisy with loud music that we couldn't relax. I wish we had done something more nature-focused there instead. It felt like a missed opportunity.

name: Linda G.
review: We did the dolphin swim in Cozumel. It was my daughter's dream, so it was worth it for her, but it felt very 'factory-like' to me. You're in and out in 30 minutes. Costa Maya ruins were much more my speed. The jungle setting is very peaceful. In Roatan, we just took a taxi to the West End village and walked around. It has a very laid-back, diver vibe. Lots of cute little cafes and docks. It felt much more authentic than the other two ports. I would have liked to stay there for dinner, but the ship left too early. All three ports were very easy to navigate in English, which made things stress-free.

name: Elodie Martin
review: Costa Maya surprised me in a good way because we left the port area quickly and found a quieter beach. The port itself didn't feel authentic. Roatan had lush scenery but also felt a bit chaotic when disembarking. Cozumel was organized but very crowded with multiple ships in port at the same time.

name: S_Gupta_99
review: Costa Maya was beautiful but the bus ride to the ruins is no joke. It's long and boring. Once you get there, the history is fascinating, but be prepared for the heat. There is almost no shade at the site. Roatan was much more relaxing. We went to Daniel Johnson's Monkey and Sloth Hangout. It was well organized and the animals seemed very well cared for. For Cozumel, we just did a little shopping and had some guacamole at a spot near the plaza. The port was very busy with four ships, so everything took longer than expected. Security lines to get back on the ship were quite long in Cozumel compared to the other two stops.

name: Jim_and_Pam
review: We really enjoyed the chocolate factory in Roatan. It's a small operation but you get to taste so many different varieties. We bought way too much to bring home! Cozumel was our day for a private boat charter. It was expensive but having the snorkel spots to ourselves before the big excursion boats arrived was worth every penny. Costa Maya was the only 'meh' day. We just stayed in the port pool. It's a nice pool, but it's loud and the drinks are pricey. It felt like being at a resort in Vegas rather than Mexico. If we go back, we will definitely try to get out to the Bacalar lagoon instead of staying local. The boat timing for the charter in Cozumel was perfect.

name: Haley Rogers
review: Cozumel was fantastic for snorkeling! We headed over to Money Bar. It's an easy taxi ride from the pier and the entry is free if you eat or drink there. The gear rental was cheap and the reef right off the shore is surprisingly healthy. Lots of parrotfish and even saw a small ray. Roatan was also nice, but the pier area is a bit chaotic with everyone trying to sell you tours. We ended up just taking a water taxi to West End which was much more chill than the main cruise beach. Costa Maya was our 'stay on the ship' day. The port area there feels very artificial, like a theme park version of Mexico. We did walk out for half an hour but it was just rows of the same jewelry and souvenir shops you see at every other Caribbean stop. If you don't book a specific excursion to the ruins or a private beach club, there isn't much 'real' culture to see within walking distance of the boat.

name: Noah Williams
review: Roatan was where we felt most engaged. The excursion included multiple stops-wildlife interaction, snorkeling, and a short city tour. It felt like good value for the time. Costa Maya was more hit or miss. We visited a beach club that was nice but fairly standard. Cozumel had the most developed infrastructure, which made it easy to navigate, but also made it feel less unique. I think expectations matter a lot-if you're looking for convenience, Cozumel delivers, but if you want something different, Roatan stands out.

name: Elena Rodriguez
review: Costa Maya was a bit of a letdown for me. The port area feels very manufactured and touristy. We took a taxi to Mahahual, which was better, but the vendors there are extremely pushy, making it hard to just relax on the beach. Cozumel was much better organized. We did the underwater oxygen helmets and it was a surreal experience seeing the fish so close without needing a SCUBA certification. Roatan was beautiful but we had a major delay getting off the ship due to local port authorities, which cut our excursion time short by nearly an hour. We still managed to see the monkeys and sloths, but everything felt rushed. I'd recommend this itinerary for the scenery, but be prepared for some logistical headaches at the piers.

name: Alicia Gomez
review: Roatan ended up being my favorite stop, which surprised me. We booked a small group snorkeling trip, and the water clarity was unreal. I've snorkeled before but never saw reefs that vibrant so close to shore. The only downside was how rushed the return felt-we barely had time to dry off before heading back to the ship. In Costa Maya, we tried to explore on our own, but the port area felt very manufactured and crowded with shops. We eventually took a taxi to a quieter beach, which improved the day a lot. Cozumel felt more flexible; we just wandered downtown, grabbed drinks, and people-watched. It wasn't as visually striking as Roatan, but it felt less rushed and easier to navigate.

name: Bernice Higgins
review: The ports were nice but I felt like the excursions were overpriced for what you got. In Roatan, we paid for a 'private beach' that turned out to be packed with people from three different cruise lines. The buffet lunch was cold chicken and rice. Cozumel was better because we just walked to a local pharmacy and then a grocery store to buy real Mexican vanilla and candy. Much better prices than the 'official' shops. Costa Maya was fine, we just sat by the port pool. It's free, but the drinks are expensive. The time in port was enough for us, honestly, we were ready to get back to the AC by 2 PM.

name: Pat_H_1955
review: Costa Maya was disappointing. Too much construction and the port area is very confusing to navigate. We tried to find the taxi stand and ended up walking in circles for twenty minutes. Cozumel was much better. We did a glass bottom boat tour which was perfect for us since we don't swim well. Saw lots of coral and even an old shipwreck. Roatan was lovely but very hilly.

name: Nancy_G
review: Loved the port in Costa Maya, specifically the chocolate making demo near the back of the plaza. It's free and very educational. We also took the tram to the local village which was $4. The beach there is narrow but the restaurants have great vibes. Cozumel felt a bit too commercialized this time around. We've been there many times and it seems like the prices for taxis just keep going up. Roatan remains my favorite because of the lush landscape, though the humidity was nearly unbearable the day we visited.

name: Jake_Midwest
review: Roatan surprised me in a good way. We booked a snorkeling and beach combo and the reef there seemed healthier than I expected. Costa Maya we did the Mayan ruins, which were interesting but the bus ride was long and early. Cozumel we just stayed near the port and shopped, nothing too memorable honestly.

name: Hiroshi Tanaka
review: The port in Costa Maya is very beautiful but very expensive. 15 dollars for a margarita is more than I pay in Tokyo! We enjoyed the Cozumel ruins at San Gervasio, they are smaller than the ones in Costa Maya but very peaceful. Roatan was very green and lush, we enjoyed the botanical gardens.

name: Hannah Goldberg
review: I've cruised a few times and this itinerary was decent but not perfect. Roatan stood out because we booked a private driver who customized the day-snorkeling, a short hike, and lunch at a local spot. That felt authentic. Costa Maya, on the other hand, felt like it was built purely for cruise traffic. We walked beyond the port and found a quieter beach, but it took effort. Cozumel was predictable but enjoyable. We did a catamaran snorkel, which was fun but definitely crowded. Timing at each port felt slightly uneven, with Costa Maya having more time than we needed and Cozumel not quite enough.

name: K-Smith_Travels
review: Roatan's West End is a must-see! We took a water taxi from West Bay and it was the best $5 we spent. It felt much more authentic than the cruise port area. We had a great lunch at a little hole-in-the-wall place overlooking the water. In Cozumel, we went to Paradise Beach. It was $65 for the all-inclusive pass which felt worth it for the pool and the service, but the ocean was a bit rocky. Costa Maya was the only disappointment. We tried to find a local craft market but it's mostly just mass-produced souvenirs. The dolphin encounter at the port looked sad to me, so we didn't stay long.

name: Mateo_Cruises
review: The port in Costa Maya is basically a theme park. It's fun for an hour but then you realize everything is priced in US dollars and is twice as expensive as it should be. We took a taxi to the local village and enjoyed a much cheaper beer on the beach. Cozumel is much the same unless you get out of the downtown area. We rented a car in Cozumel and drove to the 'wild side'-no electricity, just waves and small beach bars. It was spectacular. Roatan was the most natural feeling of the three. We did a botanical garden tour that was very educational and saw some beautiful tropical flowers.

name: Carly_Sunshine
review: We had a blast in Cozumel doing the electric bike tour. It takes you along the coast away from the main town and you get to see some of the smaller ruins on the island. It's much cooler than sitting on a bus. Roatan was also great; we did the 'Little French Key' day trip. It was a bit pricey but it was so peaceful and the lunch was delicious-fresh lobster and coconut rice. Costa Maya was the only 'meh' day. We did the Bacalar Lagoon tour, which was a very long drive. The lagoon is stunning, the 'seven colors of blue' are real, but I spent more time on a bus than I did in the water. If you don't mind long travel times, it's worth it, but if you want to relax, maybe pick something closer to the pier. Overall, a great mix of activities across the three stops. I felt like I got a good taste of both Mexico and Honduras.

name: Nina Caldwell
review: In Roatan we booked a zipline and animal sanctuary combo which ended up being the most memorable part of the trip. The zipline went over thick jungle and then we stopped to see sloths and monkeys up close. The guides were friendly and kept things moving without feeling rushed. Costa Maya was more laid back. We grabbed a taxi to a beach club just outside the main port area and spent the afternoon in the water and under shade. It was not fancy but it was peaceful and easy to enjoy. In Cozumel we walked around the port area first, then took a short ride to a snorkeling spot. The water was clear but currents made it tricky for beginners in our group. I would say Roatan had the best balance of activity and nature, while Costa Maya was best for pure relaxation and Cozumel was somewhere in between.

name: Tom_H_66
review: For our day in Cozumel, we booked a private catamaran. Best decision ever. We got away from the cruise crowds and had a private reef to ourselves. The crew caught fresh conch and made ceviche right on the boat. It was the highlight of the trip. In Costa Maya, we did the tequila seminar. It was educational, though they really push you to buy the expensive bottles at the end. Roatan was our least favorite. We tried to do a walking tour but it was so hot and the sidewalks were uneven. We ended up just heading back to the ship for a nap. I think next time I'd book a water-based excursion for Roatan since being on land was just too humid for us.

name: D_O_Sullivan
review: In Cozumel, we did the bar hop tour to the east side. It was a great way to see the undeveloped parts of the island away from the tourist traps. Our guide was local and had so many stories about the island's history. We didn't do much in Costa Maya, just grabbed a couple of drinks at the port pool. It's a nice facility but very expensive compared to local spots. Roatan was our snorkeling day. The reef there is in much better shape than the ones I've seen in the Virgin Islands. We saw a sea turtle and several stingrays. My only gripe with the itinerary is the early departure from Roatan. 3:00 PM is just too early to get back on the ship when there is so much to see on the island. You really only get half a day there which is a shame.

name: Camila Torres
review: Roatan ended up being our favorite stop, mostly because we booked a small-group island tour that included a wildlife sanctuary and a quiet beach on the other side of the island. The drive itself was eye-opening, seeing neighborhoods beyond the cruise port area. Holding a sloth felt surreal, even if it was clearly set up for tourists. The beach portion was relaxed and not overcrowded, which we appreciated.  Costa Maya was more frustrating. We tried to do our own thing and walk beyond the port, but it felt a bit disorganized once outside. We ended up at a beach club that was fine but nothing memorable. Cozumel felt the easiest to navigate. We just grabbed a taxi downtown, wandered shops, and had lunch by the water. It was simple but enjoyable.

name: S_Kim_Adventures
review: Costa Maya ruins were the highlight. Chacchoben is stunning and the trees provide a lot of shade which was needed. Our guide was a local and told us so much about the plants and animals too. Roatan was a bit of a mess for us because our excursion was cancelled last minute, so we just wandered around the port. It's okay but fairly limited. Cozumel snorkeling was top notch. We saw a sea turtle and several rays. The water is so blue it doesn't look real. Great trip for photographers.

name: Sarah Jenkins
review: First time cruiser here. Roatan was stunningly green. We did the sloth and monkey hang-out and it was the best part of the whole trip. The animals seem well cared for and the guides were very helpful with photos. In Costa Maya, we did the lost Mayan kingdom water park. It was fun for the kids, but honestly, it's something you could do anywhere. I regret not seeing the actual ruins instead. Cozumel was extremely crowded with four other ships in port. We tried to go to a public beach but it was packed, so we just headed back to the ship early. Next time I'll book a private beach club in advance for Cozumel.

name: BeachLover88
review: Cozumel was fantastic! We spent the day at Mr. Sancho's. It was a bit crowded because there were four ships in port, but the service was fast and the pool was refreshing. My kids loved the inflatable water park. In Roatan, we did the monkey and sloth hangout. My daughter is still talking about holding the sloth. It was a short excursion, which was nice because we had time to walk through the shops at the pier afterward. Costa Maya was our 'stay on the ship' day. We'd been there before and find the port area too artificial, and we weren't up for a long bus ride to the ruins this time around. The kids enjoyed having the ship slides to themselves.

name: Aditi Sharma
review: I was really looking forward to the ruins in Costa Maya, but the tour was cancelled due to a mechanical issue with the bus. We were pretty bummed. We ended up just staying in the port area which is basically one big mall. In Cozumel, we did the chocolate tasting and it was actually very educational. I didn't realize how much history goes into it! Roatan was the best for nature. We did a botanical garden walk and saw some amazing birds. I just wish the ports weren't so geared towards selling you plastic trinkets. The natural beauty of Honduras is stunning, but you have to look past the tourist traps to find it. Next time I'd book a private car in Roatan to see the East End where it's supposedly much quieter. Cozumel is still the king of shopping though.

name: Derek Vogel
review: Roatan is beautiful but the poverty is very visible once you leave the tourist areas. It's a bit of an eye-opener. The beach at Tabyana was nice but overcrowded. In Cozumel, we did the tequila seminar. It was informative, though clearly a sales pitch at the end. The food provided was actually the best meal of the trip. Costa Maya felt like a tourist trap. Everything is priced in USD and quite expensive for Mexico. We tried to walk to the local village but it was further than it looked in the heat. Next time I'd book a proper excursion there or just stay on the boat and enjoy the empty pool.

name: Isabella Rossi
review: Costa Maya ended up being our favorite because we booked a smaller, more intimate experience away from the main port. Roatan was beautiful but felt rushed with the excursion schedule we chose. Cozumel was fun but busy, especially near the main shopping areas. I think the key with this itinerary is picking the right excursions for your preferences.

name: Tabitha_Cruise
review: Costa Maya had way too much seaweed on the beach in Mahahual. It smelled pretty bad so we didn't stay long. We went back to the port and used the pool there, which was crowded but clean. Roatan was the highlight. We went to a place called Maya Key which is just a short boat ride from the pier. It has a nice beach, a small zoo, and some replica ruins. It was very convenient and didn't feel as rushed as other excursions. Cozumel was fine, just did some basic shopping for silver and leather goods. The prices are better if you walk a few blocks away from the waterfront.

name: Evan Morales
review: Roatan ended up being the most memorable stop for us because we booked a small snorkeling excursion that took us out to a calmer reef area. The water visibility was surprisingly good and the guide kept things organized so we weren't rushed. Costa Maya felt more like a controlled shopping area unless you had a pre-booked tour, so we mostly just walked around the port complex there. In Cozumel, we grabbed a taxi into town and wandered the central square and waterfront, which was easy but very crowded with other cruise groups. I'd say Roatan had the best balance of activity and time, while the other two felt more dependent on planning ahead.

name: Fatima Al-Sayed
review: The ports were a mixed bag. Cozumel felt very safe and easy to navigate. We walked to the local museum and had coffee in the square. It was peaceful. Costa Maya felt like a giant souvenir shop. Every time we turned around, someone was trying to sell us a massage or a tequila tasting. It was very high-pressure. In Roatan, we had a bit of a scare when our tour van got a flat tire on the way back from the iguana farm. The driver handled it well and got a replacement vehicle quickly, but we were worried about missing the ship. I'd recommend only using reputable tour companies there because the infrastructure isn't great. The iguana farm was interesting though, hundreds of them just roaming around.

name: Aisha Khan
review: Roatan felt the most vibrant culturally. Our guide pointed out schools, markets, and different communities, which added context beyond just activities. Costa Maya was more about the excursion itself-we visited ruins and learned about Mayan history, which I appreciated, but the experience felt somewhat scripted. Cozumel was very tourist-forward, but I still enjoyed a beach club where the water was calm and clear. I noticed that Cozumel had the most crowd overlap with other ships, which made certain areas feel congested. Overall, I valued Roatan the most because it felt like we actually saw the island rather than just passing through.

name: Jordan P.
review: Roatan was the highlight for us. We booked a private driver named Victor who took us all over the island before the crowds hit the West End. The greenery is stunning, though the traffic near the port at Coxen Hole is absolutely no joke. We spent about three hours at West Bay Beach and the snorkeling right off the shore was some of the best I've seen in the Caribbean. We did find the vendors a bit pushy there, but a polite 'no' usually worked. In Cozumel, we decided to skip the organized excursions and just rented a jeep to drive to the 'wild side' of the island. It was so much better than the crowded pier area. We stopped at Coconuts for a drink and just enjoyed the view of the waves hitting the rocks. The contrast between the two sides of the island is crazy. Definitely felt like we had enough time in both places, but I wish the Costa Maya stop was longer because by the time we got back from the ruins, we had zero time to explore the actual port shops or the pool area.

name: Marissa Delgado
review: Roatan was our favorite stop on this itinerary. We booked a guided island tour that included a visit to a sloth and monkey sanctuary, a short scenic drive over the hills, and a beach break at the end. The animal encounter was the highlight because the guides explained a lot about conservation and how tourism supports local work. After that we went to a small local beach where the water was calm and clear, and we had about an hour to swim before heading back. Costa Maya felt very different. The port area was built up and easy to navigate, but we chose to leave the immediate shopping zone and take a taxi to a quieter beach club. It was less crowded and we appreciated having space to relax instead of being surrounded by cruise crowds. The ride there was short, maybe fifteen minutes, and the driver pointed out small villages along the way. Cozumel was our most active day. We rented a private driver and did a mix of snorkeling and a quick stop near a beach club area. The snorkeling spot had decent visibility but currents picked up later in the morning so we did not stay long. Overall, I liked how each port offered a different pace: Roatan for nature and animals, Costa Maya for a relaxed beach day, and Cozumel for activity and exploring.

name: Miguel Santos
review: Roatan had the best mix of nature and activity. We did a guided tour that included a viewpoint, local market, and beach stop. It felt like we saw more of the island beyond the typical tourist spots.  Costa Maya was more hit or miss. The beach we went to was nice, but getting there involved some confusion with taxis and timing.  Cozumel was very straightforward. Good for a relaxed day without much planning.

name: D_Chen82
review: Had an okay time in Costa Maya. We did the Chacchoben ruins tour. The history is fascinating and the guides really know their stuff, but be warned: the bus ride is nearly an hour each way and the humidity in the jungle is intense. I wish we had more time to explore the site because it felt like we were being herded back to the bus just as I started getting good photos. In Cozumel, we just walked to a local spot for fish tacos and did some light shopping. It's a very easy port to navigate on your own if you don't want to spend $100 on a scheduled tour.

name: Priya Shah
review: Each port had a very different feel which I appreciated. Roatan felt more natural and less built up once you left the port. We did a wildlife and beach combo tour which was fun but also raised some questions for me about how the animals are treated. Costa Maya felt very commercial unless you go far out, which we didn't. Cozumel was the easiest to explore independently. We rented bikes and rode along the coast, stopping whenever we wanted. That flexibility made it my favorite day even though Roatan was probably more visually impressive.

name: Andre Wallace
review: Roatan ended up being the most memorable stop for us. We booked a snorkeling trip through a smaller local operator, and the water clarity was unreal. It didn't feel overly commercial once we got away from the immediate port. Costa Maya was a bit of a letdown in comparison. The port area felt like a controlled shopping zone, and we didn't book an excursion, which I think was a mistake. Cozumel was easier to manage since taxis were straightforward, but it was definitely the busiest port of the three.

name: Derrick Lawson
review: Roatan was mostly about the sloth sanctuary for us. We did a short guided visit and it was interesting to hear how the animals are rescued and cared for. The rest of the island tour was fine but not as memorable. Costa Maya we stayed close to the port and just explored the shops and small pools in the area. It was convenient but felt very touristy so we did not stay long. In Cozumel we took a taxi to a local beach instead of an organized excursion. It was a simple day with swimming and sitting under umbrellas. Nothing overly structured, which was actually nice after several busy stops.

name: Marcus & Jen
review: We loved the history in Costa Maya! The Mayan ruins at Chacchoben are a must-see if you haven't been. Our guide, Ivan, was so passionate and pointed out spider monkeys in the trees above the temples. It felt very Indiana Jones. Cozumel was a bit of a contrast. We did the Jeep tour around the island. The east side of the island is much more rugged and beautiful than the side where the ships dock. No electricity over there, just wild waves and small beach bars. Roatan was our relaxation day. We went to Little French Key. It's a bit pricey to get out there, but the water is calm and the lunch was fantastic-fresh lobster and coconut rice. One thing to note: the pier in Roatan is very long, so be prepared for a walk if you don't use the 'magic chair' lift.

name: Lucas Pereira
review: This itinerary really depends on how much planning you do ahead of time. In Roatan, we booked a private driver instead of a large group excursion, which made a huge difference. We were able to stop at a couple of scenic overlooks, a small beach stretch, and even a local area where it felt like everyday life was still going on outside the tourism zones. That flexibility made Roatan feel the most authentic of the three stops. Costa Maya, however, felt very controlled in comparison. We didn't book an excursion there and ended up staying inside the port complex longer than planned. It was clean and organized, but it didn't feel like we saw anything beyond the immediate cruise area. Cozumel was somewhere in the middle for us. We walked into town and explored a few streets, but the heat and crowds made it less comfortable to linger. Transportation back to the ship was easy, but the overall experience felt more tourist-heavy than immersive. If I were to redo this itinerary, I'd prioritize pre-booking something meaningful in Costa Maya and allow more structured exploration in Roatan, because the contrast between planned and unplanned days really shaped how each port felt.

name: Alicia Nguyen
review: Roatan we did a guided tour that included a sloth and monkey sanctuary and a short beach visit. The animals were the main reason we chose it and it did not disappoint. Costa Maya we went to a beach club about fifteen minutes away from the port and it was much quieter than expected with plenty of space to relax. Cozumel we booked a snorkeling excursion that had good visibility but felt slightly rushed due to multiple stops and other boats around. Still, we saw a lot of marine life and enjoyed the day overall.

name: Ayesha Khan
review: Our trip to the Chacchoben ruins from Costa Maya was incredible. Our guide, Ivan, was so knowledgeable about Mayan history and made the long bus ride fly by with stories. The ruins themselves are breathtaking, especially since you can still see where the jungle is reclaiming some of the structures. It was a bit hot and humid, so bring plenty of water. In Cozumel, we did a chocolate making workshop which was fun for the kids, but I felt it was a bit overpriced for what it was. We skipped Roatan entirely because the weather looked shaky and we wanted to enjoy the quiet ship.

name: Marcus L
review: We tried to maximize each port and honestly it got exhausting. Roatan was a full-day excursion with multiple stops, Costa Maya was an early morning ruins trip, and by Cozumel we were worn out. Cozumel ended up being a simple walk around and early return to the ship. If I did this itinerary again, I'd plan at least one low-key port day.

name: Lars Nielsen
review: I really enjoyed the history at Chacchoben in Costa Maya. Our guide was actually of Mayan descent and told us stories passed down through his family. It's a long day though, especially with the bus ride. Cozumel is just too crowded for me these days. Every time I go, there are more people and more vendors yelling at you to buy t-shirts. Roatan is still the gem of this itinerary. The greenery and the hills are beautiful as you sail in. We did a catamaran sail there that was very peaceful.

name: Sophie Nguyen
review: We're not big on excursions, so we judged the ports based on what you can do independently. Cozumel wins for that. It's very easy to get around and find things at your own pace. Roatan was trickier without a plan, so we ended up joining a last-minute tour. Costa Maya felt the most limited unless you committed to an excursion ahead of time. If you like structure, it's fine, but spontaneous travelers might find it frustrating.

name: Derek Holloway
review: Roatan had a solid snorkeling excursion but the transfer process from ship to boat took longer than expected. Costa Maya was disappointing without an excursion since we mostly stayed in the port complex and didn't see much else. Cozumel was more flexible, and we took a taxi to a quieter beach area which ended up being the best part of that stop. This itinerary really seems to depend on how much you plan ahead.

name: Tomislav Petrovic
review: Roatan felt the most authentic. We hired a guide at the port and he showed us parts of the island that weren't just tourist spots. Costa Maya felt overly staged, especially near the port entrance. Cozumel had better infrastructure, but also more crowds. I enjoyed the variety across the stops though.

name: Amelia Chen
review: This itinerary gave a good mix, but I think your experience depends heavily on what you book. In Roatan, we chose a smaller, locally run tour and it made all the difference. The guide shared personal stories and took us to less crowded spots. Costa Maya felt more generic, even though the ruins themselves were impressive. The logistics there-long bus rides, early departures-made the day feel tiring. Cozumel was the easiest to navigate and had the most options, but also the most people. If I had to rank them, Roatan first for authenticity, Cozumel second for convenience, and Costa Maya last due to the effort required.

name: Hector Morales
review: Roatan we booked a private island tour that included a sloth encounter and a stop at a local beach. The drive through the island gave us a good sense of everyday life there, not just tourist spots. Costa Maya we chose a beach club outside the port and spent most of the day swimming and eating simple local food. It was less hectic than staying near the cruise center. In Cozumel we did a snorkeling trip that felt a bit crowded but still enjoyable because the water was so clear. We saw coral and small fish pretty easily even without diving far.

name: Marcus L.
review: Roatan was incredible but the logistics were a bit of a headache. We booked the shipwreck snorkel and while the reef was pristine, the bus drive from the pier took nearly an hour due to some local construction. It felt like we only got 45 minutes in the water before we had to dry off and head back. Cozumel was a much smoother experience; we just walked off the boat and grabbed a taxi to the town square. Had some of the best street tacos of my life and did a bit of silver shopping. Costa Maya was purely a beach day for us at the port pool. It's convenient if you don't want to deal with the hassle of excursions, but it definitely feels more like a theme park than a destination. I wish we had more time in Roatan to actually see the island instead of just sitting in traffic.

name: Anika Patel
review: Cozumel felt the most developed and easiest to explore independently. We walked around town, did some shopping, and had lunch without needing a structured plan. Roatan was more about organized excursions, and we enjoyed a guided island tour that included scenic stops and a short beach break. Costa Maya was the only port where we felt unsure what to do without an excursion, so we didn't spend much time off the ship there.

name: Isabella-Cruises
review: The ports were a mixed bag. I loved the history in Costa Maya-the ruins are a must-see even if the drive is long. Roatan was stunning but we had a bad experience with a local taxi driver who tried to overcharge us at the end of the day. It left a bit of a sour taste in my mouth. Cozumel was the most professional; everything is streamlined for tourists. We did the submarine tour and it was fascinating to see the reef from 100 feet down. I think the itinerary is good, but you have to be careful in Roatan if you aren't on an official ship excursion. The time spent in each port was mostly okay, but we felt very rushed in Costa Maya because the ruins tour takes up almost the whole window. I'd love an extra two hours there just to relax after the long bus ride back.

name: Ayesha Khan
review: The timing in Cozumel was frustrating. We didn't dock until 1:00 PM, which meant most of the good morning snorkeling tours were already done. We ended up just taking a taxi to the town square. Roatan was much better scheduled. We had a full day and spent it at Little French Key. It's a bit expensive but very beautiful and secluded. The lunch included was authentic island food-rice and beans with jerk chicken. Costa Maya was a bit of a letdown. The 'Tequila Tasting' we did was mostly just a sales pitch to buy expensive bottles. I've had better experiences in other Caribbean ports.

name: Linda G.
review: Cozumel is always a favorite. We went to Mr. Sanchos for the day. It's an all-inclusive beach club and they really take care of you. The food was surprisingly good for a buffet and the drinks kept coming. It was very crowded though, so if you want peace and quiet, this isn't it. Roatan was beautiful but the pier at Coxen Hole is very industrial looking. We did a catamaran snorkel trip and saw some great coral. The crew was fun but the equipment was a bit dated. Costa Maya was our last stop. We just walked the pier and did some souvenir shopping. The walk from the ship to the actual port exit is very long, especially in the heat, so take the little tram if it's running. Overall, a solid itinerary but I felt like the port times were a little short for Roatan.

name: Kathy_G_61
review: I struggled with the walking in Costa Maya. The pier is huge and the shuttle was full. Once in the port, it's all cobblestones which was hard for my walker. Cozumel was much more accessible. We took a van to the dolphin encounter and it was very well managed for people with mobility issues. Roatan was a bit of a challenge too, very hilly. We stayed in the port area and looked at the shops. The crafts in Roatan were much more unique than the stuff in Mexico-lots of beautiful wood carvings. I wish the cruise line provided more information about the walking distances at each pier before we got off.

name: Sarah J.
review: Did the Chacchoben ruins in Costa Maya. The bus ride was nearly an hour each way but the guide was so knowledgeable about Mayan history that the time flew by. Seeing the pyramids poking through the jungle canopy was breathtaking. Just be prepared for the humidity! We also did a catamaran snorkel in Cozumel. The reef was okay, but I've seen better in other parts of the Caribbean. The crew made the trip fun with music and drinks on the way back, though. Roatan felt a bit rushed; our ship cleared customs late so we only had about four hours on the island, which wasn't enough to really see anything beyond the immediate port area and a quick lunch. I'd recommend prioritizing the ruins if you haven't seen them.

name: Olivia Martin
review: The pacing between ports was interesting. In Roatan, our excursion had a nice balance between activities and downtime, so we never felt rushed. Costa Maya felt more rigid. The ruins tour was informative, but everything was scheduled tightly and we didn't have much flexibility. Cozumel gave us the most freedom since we planned our own day, but it was also the busiest stop. It took some effort to find a quieter area away from the crowds. I appreciated that each port offered something different, but I definitely preferred the more relaxed structure we had in Roatan compared to the more rigid experience in Costa Maya.

name: Priya_S
review: Cozumel was great for the kids. We did the chocolate making class and they loved grinding the beans. Roatan was a bit scary with the driving, the roads are very narrow and the drivers are aggressive. We did the beach day at Tabyana and the sand was like powder. Costa Maya was our 'rest' day. We just sat by the port pool which is actually very nice and free to use. The only thing is the drinks there are ship prices, not Mexico prices. It was a good mix of ports, though I wish there was more of a cultural focus in the ship-sponsored tours rather than just beach clubs.

name: Nia Okoye
review: In Roatan, we booked a snorkeling and beach combo and the water conditions were excellent, with good visibility. Costa Maya was more of a casual stop for us since we didn't plan anything ahead, so we just stayed in the port area and relaxed. Cozumel felt like the busiest of the three ports, but we managed to find a quieter spot away from the main shopping streets and spent time just walking along the waterfront. Each stop had a very different vibe, and I think Roatan was best for activities, while Cozumel worked better for independent wandering.

name: Rafael Ortega
review: Roatan we booked a half-day island tour that included a monkey and sloth encounter and a stop at a hillside viewpoint. The guide shared a lot about local life which made the drive interesting. We did not feel rushed and had enough time for photos. Costa Maya was very relaxed for us. We took a taxi to a quieter beach club instead of staying near the port. The beach was calm, with shallow water and light crowds, which was exactly what we wanted after a busy travel day. Cozumel we chose a snorkeling excursion near a reef. The visibility was decent but there were many other groups in the water, so it felt a bit crowded. Still, we saw colorful fish and enjoyed the day overall.

name: Chris and Sam
review: We are experienced cruisers and this itinerary is a classic. We usually skip the ship excursions and book private. In Roatan, we used a local guide for a private island tour. Best decision ever. We saw the local neighborhoods and a beautiful hidden beach away from the cruise crowds. Costa Maya is still a bit of a 'fake' port to me, but the tequila tasting near the fountain was actually informative and fun. Cozumel was our 'adventure' day where we rented Jeeps and drove to the other side of the island. It's much more rugged and beautiful over there with no electricity and just small beach bars. It's a totally different vibe from the downtown area where the ships dock. I highly recommend getting away from the pier in all three of these locations if you want a real experience. The scheduling was fine, but we felt a bit rushed in Roatan.

name: Mariah J.
review: This was my third time on this itinerary. Roatan continues to be my favorite. The lush green mountains meeting the blue water is just unbeatable. We did a fishing charter this time and caught some snapper that a local place cooked up for us. Costa Maya hasn't changed much-still a tourist trap at the pier, but Mahahual is slowly getting more developed. The seaweed problem in Costa Maya seems to be getting worse every year though. Cozumel is always reliable. We did the salsa and salsa tour (making salsa and dancing salsa). It's cheesy but a lot of fun with a group of friends. The port logistics were smooth at all three stops, though the security line to get back on the ship in Cozumel was nearly 30 minutes long in the direct sun. Overall, a great trip for anyone who loves the sun, but I'd suggest more time in Roatan and less in Costa Maya if they ever change the schedule.

name: Claire Dubois
review: Roatan ended up being the highlight for us. We booked a small group excursion that included snorkeling and a short island tour, and it felt like a good mix of activity and relaxation. Costa Maya felt more like a constructed port experience, especially if you don't leave the main area. We chose not to do a long excursion there and it showed. Cozumel was easier to manage. We went to a quieter beach away from the main port, which helped avoid the crowds. Overall, I think the itinerary works best if you plan ahead, especially for Costa Maya.

name: Mark Lind
review: We booked a reef snorkeling trip in Roatan and it was well organized with good visibility underwater. Costa Maya felt like a port where excursions are almost necessary, since the immediate area is mostly shops. Cozumel was easier to navigate independently and we walked into town for a few hours before heading back. Roatan was the only stop that felt truly scenic.

name: Clara Bow
review: I loved Cozumel! We went to the Pearl Farm. It's a bit of a boat ride to get there, but it's so unique. You get to snorkel over the pearl beds and see how they grow them. Lunch was served on a deserted beach. It felt like a true escape. Costa Maya was a bit disappointing in comparison. It felt very manufactured. We did the shore excursion to the lagoon, but it was so crowded we couldn't find a lounge chair. Roatan was better; we went to a small resort called Turquoise Bay. It was quiet and the water was like glass. The only issue was the long drive across the island, which took about 45 minutes each way.

name: travel-bug-sarah
review: Costa Maya was okay but the pier is ridiculously long. If you have mobility issues, wait for the tram! We did the Chacchoben ruins and the guide was fantastic, but the 50-minute bus ride each way in a van with weak AC was rough. Cozumel was much better; we did a private Jeep tour to the wild side of the island. No electricity or crowds, just raw coastline. Roatan was beautiful but the insects are no joke-bring the heavy-duty spray.

name: V_Gomez
review: The ports were nice but very busy. Roatan had three ships in, and it felt like the island was at capacity. We did the sloth sanctuary, which was fun but very quick. Costa Maya was better for lounging. We just stayed at the port pool. It's free and actually quite large, though the drinks are pricey. Cozumel was our best day. We rented a car and drove around the whole island. The 'wild' side of the island is spectacular-no buildings, just nature and some small bars. It was nice to escape the cruise crowds for a few hours. Just make sure you fill up the gas tank before returning it, as the stations near the pier are a ripoff.

name: Daniela Costa
review: Roatan offered the most memorable experience for me. We joined a small group excursion that combined a wildlife visit and a beach stop, and it felt well paced without being rushed. Costa Maya was a bit disappointing because we didn't book anything in advance and ended up staying within the port complex, which felt artificial. Cozumel redeemed things slightly. We found a quieter beach farther from the main dock area, but it required negotiating with taxi drivers and figuring out timing to get back. Overall, I'd say planning ahead is essential for these ports.

name: Jessica Low
review: I loved the variety on this trip! Roatan had the best nature-the chocolate factory tour was so cool and the jungle smells amazing after it rains. Costa Maya was our beach day; we just sat under a palapa in Mahahual and watched the waves. It was very relaxing, though the seaweed was a bit thick in some spots. Cozumel was our big excursion day where we went to the San Gervasio ruins. They aren't as big as the ones on the mainland, but they were very peaceful and not nearly as crowded. I felt like we had plenty of time in each port, though I wish Cozumel stayed open a bit later into the evening so we could have had dinner on land. The transition from the ship to the shore was easy at all three stops, which isn't always the case. Definitely a solid itinerary for people who like a mix of history and relaxation.

name: Hargrove_Family
review: Traveling with three kids is hard but these ports made it easy. Roatan's monkey park was the biggest hit. The kids are still talking about the monkeys jumping on their heads. In Costa Maya, we just stayed at the port pool because the kids didn't want to get on another bus. It was free and kept them entertained for hours. Cozumel we did a submarine tour. It was a bit pricey but a once-in-a-lifetime thing for the little ones to see the reef without having to swim. All in all, a very family-friendly set of destinations. We didn't feel unsafe at any point, which was a concern of mine before we left. Everything was well-organized.

name: Mina K.
review: As a solo traveler, I was mostly concerned about how easy it would be to get around at each stop. Cozumel was by far the simplest-I felt comfortable walking around and finding things to do without a plan. Roatan required a bit more planning, so I joined a group excursion to avoid dealing with transportation. Costa Maya was the only place I felt slightly unsure about where to go after leaving the port area. I ended up just staying within the complex, which was fine but not very memorable.

name: Anika Patel
review: Costa Maya was the only port where I felt like time was poorly used. We did the ruins excursion and while the site itself was interesting, the long bus ride and early departure made it feel rushed and tiring. Roatan was much more enjoyable. We visited a small wildlife sanctuary and spent time at the beach after. Cozumel we just wandered around downtown, which was easy and stress-free.

name: Priya_Chopra
review: Cozumel is a diver's paradise. I did a two-tank dive at Palancar Reef and the visibility was stunning, easily 100 feet. The coral formations are huge. My husband stayed on the ship that day but joined me in Roatan for the beach. Roatan has a lot of charm but the local infrastructure is clearly struggling with the amount of tourists. Costa Maya was just a shopping day for us. We found some nice silver jewelry in one of the shops near the back of the port, though you have to haggle quite a bit to get a fair price. Overall a good mix of ports.

name: Carlos Eduardo
review: Great diving in Roatan! The reef is in much better shape than Cozumel. The dive masters were very professional and the equipment was high quality. Cozumel felt a bit 'tired'-the same shops and the same tours I saw five years ago. Costa Maya is growing fast, but the infrastructure isn't quite there. The line for taxis back to the port was nearly 40 minutes long in the blazing sun. They need more organization for the independent travelers. Still, the beach at Mahahual is beautiful if you find a spot without the sea grass.

name: Samantha Reed
review: Cozumel is the gold standard for port organization. Everything flows so well. We did a chocolate and wine tasting which was very sophisticated and tasty. Costa Maya is the opposite. It feels like you're being funneled through a maze of shops just to leave the port area. It's annoying. We eventually made it out to a small restaurant in Mahahual called Nohoch Kay for amazing fish tacos. Roatan's natural beauty is the best of the three, but the infrastructure is lacking. We went to the botanical gardens and it was lovely, but the path was very muddy and slippery. Definitely wear good shoes if you go off the beaten path in Roatan. The itinerary overall was great for seeing different sides of the Western Caribbean.

name: Mr_Henderson
review: Costa Maya was great for the Mayan Healing Ritual excursion. It was very relaxing and felt unique compared to the usual beach breaks. It's held in a small village area that felt much more 'real' than the port. In Roatan, we just stayed at the port beach (Mahogany Bay) because we didn't want to deal with the hills and the heat. It's a nice beach, but the water isn't as clear as other parts of the island. Cozumel was fine, just very busy with four other ships in port at the same time.

name: Darnell_W84
review: Roatan was the highlight for me. I did the scuba diving excursion and the reef is in incredible shape compared to other spots in the Caribbean. We saw a couple of reef sharks and a massive sea turtle. In Cozumel, we did the 'Amazing Race' style scavenger hunt through the town. It was a fun way to see the backstreets and interact with locals rather than just sitting at a bar. Costa Maya was our 'ship day'-we looked at the crowds on the pier and decided to just stay on board and enjoy the quiet pool. If you've seen one Mexican port mall, you've seen them all, and Costa Maya is the king of them.

name: Elena Rodriguez
review: Cozumel was the highlight for our group. We bypassed the standard cruise excursions and took a taxi to Punta Sur Eco Beach Park. It's about a 35-minute drive from the pier, but absolutely worth it for the lighthouse views and the crocodile spotting in the lagoon. The beach there is much quieter than the clubs closer to the ship. Roatan was also beautiful, but the pier area in Coxen Hole felt a bit chaotic with everyone trying to sell you a taxi ride. We eventually made it to West Bay for some snorkeling, which was world-class, though we felt a bit rushed to get back before the ship departed. Costa Maya was our 'stay on the ship' day. We walked around the port area for twenty minutes, but it felt like a giant, overpriced shopping mall designed just for tourists. If you aren't doing a long bus ride to the ruins, there isn't much substance right at the dock. We preferred the quiet pool on the ship instead.

name: Javier M.
review: Costa Maya ruins are a must-see! Chaccoben is amazing. The jungle setting makes you feel like Indiana Jones. The guides are very respectful of the history. Cozumel is better for water sports. We did a helmet dive which was a unique way to see the reef without needing to know how to scuba. Roatan was a bit of a mixed bag. The scenery is 10/10 but the infrastructure is struggling. We were stuck in a shuttle for 45 minutes just trying to get out of the port area. Once we got to our destination it was fine, but the logistics on that island need work.

name: Jackson_Family_5
review: We traveled with three kids and these ports were perfect for them. In Cozumel, we did the sea lion encounter at Chankanaab and they haven't stopped talking about it. The park is very well maintained. In Roatan, we did a beach day at a resort that had a big inflatable water park in the ocean. It kept them busy for hours. Costa Maya was actually quite fun for the kids too because of the big pool right in the middle of the port area. It's shallow and safe. My only complaint is the cost of food in the ports. A simple lunch for five people in Cozumel cost us nearly $120. Next time we might just head back to the ship for lunch before going back out. The port times were generous enough that we could have done that if we had planned better.

name: Kwame Akoto
review: Wasn't a fan of the Costa Maya port. It's basically a maze of souvenir shops that you have to walk through to get anywhere. We ended up just taking a quick taxi to Mahahual for some street tacos which were excellent, but the beach there had a lot of seaweed when we visited. Cozumel was a much smoother experience. We did the America's Cup 12-meter regatta excursion and it was exhilarating to actually help sail those boats. Roatan was nice but very humid. We did a glass-bottom boat tour because my wife doesn't like to swim, and we still saw plenty of coral and fish. The pier in Roatan is quite long, so be prepared for a bit of a hike if you aren't using the chairlift thing they have there.

name: Maya Lopez
review: Cozumel worked really well for us because we didn't want a structured day. We just wandered and found a small beach club that wasn't too busy. Costa Maya was the opposite-we booked a cooking class excursion and that ended up being one of the more memorable experiences. Very hands-on and the group was small. Roatan was beautiful but I wish we had more time there. It felt like we barely scratched the surface before needing to head back.

name: Robert L. Miller
review: I'm a bit of a history buff, so I was looking forward to the ruins. Chacchoben in Costa Maya didn't disappoint. The climbable sections are limited now to preserve them, but the scale is still impressive. Cozumel felt too commercialized for me. It's basically one giant pharmacy and jewelry store after another. We took a ferry to Playa del Carmen but the crossing was very rough-lots of seasick passengers. Roatan was the most authentic-feeling stop. We visited a local school as part of a 'giving back' excursion. It was humbling and much better than sitting on a beach. The logistics in Roatan were a bit messy with the bus dispatch, but the experience itself was the highlight of my cruise. Wish we had stayed later in Mexico to see the sunset.

name: Niels_J
review: I was looking for history and found it in Costa Maya. The Chacchoben ruins are very impressive and you can still climb some of the smaller structures. Our guide was excellent. Cozumel was too commercial for me. It felt like every square inch was designed to sell me a t-shirt or a diamond ring. Roatan was better, but the pier at Coxen Hole is very cramped and chaotic. We did the sloth encounter which was cute, but the tour felt a bit like an assembly line moving people through as fast as possible. I would have liked more time to just sit and enjoy the jungle.

name: Harold T.
review: Cozumel was our best day. We took a taxi to a quieter beach area and spent hours swimming and relaxing without feeling rushed. Roatan had great scenery, but our excursion felt a bit packed schedule-wise. Costa Maya was the only port where we decided to stay on the ship after getting off briefly-it just didn't appeal to us compared to the other stops.

name: Noah Bernstein
review: I've done a similar itinerary before and this one felt pretty typical. Roatan stood out again because we hired a private driver who took us to less crowded areas, including a quiet beach and a small local restaurant. Costa Maya felt very geared toward tourists. Even outside the port, it didn't feel like we were seeing much beyond what was set up for visitors. Cozumel had the most options, but also the most congestion. We did a snorkeling trip there and it felt a bit like a production line. Overall, Roatan felt the most authentic, while the other two required more effort to find something that didn't feel overly commercial.

name: Dylan Carter
review: We really enjoyed Roatan because we booked a smaller group excursion that combined snorkeling and sightseeing. It didn't feel rushed, which was nice. Costa Maya was harder to navigate independently, so we ended up staying near the port longer than expected. Cozumel was easy to get around, even without a plan.

name: Mariah_C
review: We did the cooking class in Cozumel and it was the best thing we did all week. We learned to make three different types of salsa and authentic ceviche. The chef was hilarious. In Roatan, we just went to the beach. It was pretty but very crowded. I think every single person on the ship went to the same beach. Costa Maya was a bit of a bore for us, we just did some souvenir shopping and went back on. I think I would skip Costa Maya next time or book a much longer tour to see something unique.

name: Isabella Rossi
review: I went into this cruise mostly interested in cultural experiences, and the ports delivered that unevenly but still memorably. Roatan exceeded expectations because we booked a small-group excursion that included a visit to a local community, a short jungle walk, and time near the water. It felt immersive without being overwhelming. Costa Maya was more complicated. The ruins were fascinating and visually striking, but the long transportation time made the day feel dominated by logistics rather than exploration. Cozumel, while more commercial, offered flexibility. We opted out of excursions and created our own plan, which worked well but required some research beforehand. I noticed that crowd levels significantly impacted enjoyment, especially in Cozumel where multiple ships were docked. Overall, I appreciated the variety, but planning ahead was key to getting the most out of each stop.

name: Omar El-Sayed
review: Roatan surprised me in a good way. We did a cultural tour that included a small village visit and lunch, which felt more meaningful than just going to a beach. Costa Maya was more frustrating because of aggressive vendors near the port area. Cozumel was easy to navigate, though, and we enjoyed just walking around without a strict plan.

name: Ellie Rodriguez
review: Costa Maya was beautiful but we felt very pressured by the vendors as soon as we stepped off the ship. We ended up taking a taxi to Mahahual for $4 per person. It was much more relaxed once we got away from the main cruise terminal. The beach there is stunning but the seagrass was a bit heavy the day we visited. Cozumel was much better for snorkeling; we went to Money Bar and just swam out from the shore. You don't even need a boat there to see some amazing fish. Roatan was okay, but we found the port area quite confusing to navigate and the excursion we had booked was cancelled at the last minute, so we just ended up walking around the local shops which wasn't very exciting.

name: Meghan Foster
review: Roatan was mostly about the animal sanctuary for us and it ended up being a really good decision. The sloths were adorable and the guides were knowledgeable. Costa Maya we stayed near the port and walked around but it felt very commercial so we did not stay long. Cozumel we took a short taxi ride to a beach area and relaxed under umbrellas for a few hours. It was a calm and easy day overall.

name: Logan Pierce
review: First time cruising and I didn't realize how different each port would feel. Roatan felt more natural, less built up. We did ziplining and it was a highlight. Costa Maya felt like a controlled environment. We stayed near the port and it didn't feel very authentic. Cozumel was busy but had more to do without booking anything in advance.

name: Samuel L. Davis
review: The itinerary was decent, but the time in port felt short. In Cozumel, we barely had enough time to finish our lunch at a local cafe before we had to run back. Roatan was the highlight; the monkeys at the sanctuary were so fun to interact with. Costa Maya is a beautiful port, very well-maintained, but it feels a bit like a movie set rather than a real place in Mexico. Overall, a good trip, but I wish we had 2-3 more hours in each location to really explore.

name: Olivia Hart
review: This was my first cruise and I wasn't sure what to expect from the ports. Roatan felt very lush and different from anything I've experienced before. We did snorkeling and saw a lot of marine life. Costa Maya was more structured since we booked a ruins excursion. The ruins were impressive, but the long bus ride made it feel rushed. Cozumel was my favorite for relaxing. We found a quieter beach area and just stayed there most of the day without worrying about a schedule.

name: Sarah_CruiseLover82
review: Cozumel is always a favorite for our family. We headed straight to Paradise Beach. It's $68 for the all-inclusive pass now, which felt a bit steep, but the service was top-notch and the kids loved the inflatable water park. The taxi ride was easy and only cost about $16 for the four of us. Roatan was beautiful but the traffic is getting out of hand. It took us nearly 45 minutes to get back from the monkey sanctuary, and we were starting to get nervous about the all-aboard time. Costa Maya was okay, but the walk from the ship to the actual port exit is incredibly long, especially in that humidity. We mostly just did some light shopping for silver and vanilla before heading back. Not a bad trip, but I wish we had more time in Roatan to actually see the island instead of just sitting in a van.

name: DeAndre Hills
review: Avoid the 'all-inclusive' beach breaks in Cozumel if you want a quiet day. We went to one that was wall-to-wall people and the music was so loud we couldn't even talk. It felt like a spring break party. On the other hand, Roatan was very peaceful. We hired a private driver named Ronny who took us all over the island, including some local spots away from the tourists. He took us to a small hilltop restaurant with a view of the whole harbor. Costa Maya was okay, but the port feels very fake. It's basically a maze designed to make you walk past every single shop before you can reach the exit to the street.

name: Elena_R
review: Costa Maya snorkeling was a bit disappointing due to the seagrass, but the beach club staff worked hard to clear it. In Cozumel, we did the chocolate and tequila tour which was informative and tasty. Roatan was definitely the winner for natural beauty. We just took a taxi to the West End and walked around. It has a very laid-back, backpacker vibe that I loved. The local food there was much better than the buffet options at the organized beach clubs. I felt like the 8 hours we had in each port was generally enough, though Cozumel gets a bit repetitive if you aren't doing a specific activity like diving or visiting ruins.

name: Clara_H_99
review: I'm a solo traveler and I felt very safe in all three ports. In Roatan, I joined a group tour for the glass-bottom boat. The reef is spectacular and you don't even have to get wet. Cozumel was easy to navigate on foot, I just spent the afternoon at the museum and then had some coffee at a local cafe. Costa Maya was the only place I felt a bit uneasy because the taxi drivers are very aggressive when you walk out of the port gates. I ended up just going back inside the port area and sitting by the pool. The scheduling was decent, though we arrived in Cozumel very early (7:00 AM) and nothing was open yet. It would be better if we arrived a bit later and stayed into the evening so we could see the nightlife.

name: AdventureSeeker88
review: I was really looking forward to Roatan but the weather didn't cooperate. It rained most of the morning so our ziplining excursion was canceled. We ended up just taking a taxi to a chocolate factory which was okay, but a bit of a 'tourist trap' feel. Cozumel saved the trip though! We rented a Jeep and drove to the other side of the island. It's completely undeveloped and rugged-no electricity, just small bars on the beach. It felt like a totally different world compared to the busy cruise terminal. We found a small spot called Coconuts on a cliff and the view was breathtaking. Costa Maya was fine, we just did the pool at the port which was free and actually quite nice. I liked that I could see the ship while I was swimming. Just watch out for the drink prices at the port bars, they are higher than on the ship!

name: Chris & Dana
review: Traveling as a couple, we preferred slower-paced days. Cozumel worked perfectly for that. We went to a quieter beach club and spent hours just relaxing.  Roatan was more activity-focused. We did a combo excursion and felt a bit rushed between stops.  Costa Maya didn't leave much of an impression. Next time we'd plan something more structured.

name: Marcus Chen
review: Cozumel was the absolute highlight for our group. We bypassed the typical ship excursions and booked a private Jeep tour that took us to the 'wild side' of the island. There's no electricity on that side, just these incredible rugged beaches and small bars like Coconuts. It felt like a completely different world compared to the crowded pier. Roatan was also great; we did the zip-lining through the jungle. The views from the top were breathtaking, though the bus ride to the site was a bit bumpy and the local traffic is definitely a concern if you're on a tight schedule. We skipped Costa Maya entirely and stayed on the ship to enjoy the quiet decks. From what we heard from others, the port area there is just a big shopping mall anyway, so I don't feel like we missed much. Overall, the time in Cozumel felt perfect, but I wish we had an extra hour in Roatan to see the west end beaches properly.

name: Svetlana Ivanova
review: We approached each port differently and that made a big difference. In Cozumel, we booked a smaller beach club that limited capacity, which helped avoid the crowds. Roatan was more of a guided experience for us, with a mix of sightseeing and water activities. Costa Maya was the most difficult to navigate independently. Transportation outside the port wasn't as straightforward, and I wish we had arranged something in advance. The ruins were interesting, but the time spent traveling there reduced the overall enjoyment. I would say Roatan felt the most balanced, Cozumel the most convenient, and Costa Maya required the most effort to enjoy.

name: Linda_and_Bob
review: We are experienced cruisers so we usually skip the big bus tours. In Cozumel, we rented a car for the day. It's very easy to navigate the island as it's basically one big loop. We found a secluded beach on the east side and had it all to ourselves for two hours. Just watch out for the moped renters; they drive a bit crazy. In Costa Maya, we actually stayed in the port and used the pool. It was crowded but convenient since we didn't want to deal with a long day. Roatan was a bit of a struggle. We tried to do a walking tour but the hills are very steep and there aren't many sidewalks once you leave the immediate port area. We ended up just grabbing a taxi back. If you go to Roatan, definitely plan for transportation. Don't think you can just wander around on foot like you can in some parts of Cozumel. The port schedule was okay, but I wish we had stayed later in Cozumel to see the sunset from the shore.

name: Isabella DeLuca
review: I tend to prefer cultural and historical experiences, so I had mixed feelings about this itinerary. Roatan surprised me because we booked a small group tour that included a visit to a local area and a short nature walk, which felt more immersive than expected. Costa Maya was probably the most educational stop because of the ruins, but the logistics made it tiring. The early departure and long drive took away from the overall experience, even though the site itself was impressive. Cozumel was the most flexible port, and we chose to explore on our own instead of booking anything. That worked well, but it did require some planning ahead to avoid the most crowded areas. I think this itinerary works best if you're intentional about what you book at each stop.

name: DeShawn Carter
review: Roatan had the best excursion options by far. We did a combination of snorkeling and a short cultural tour, and it felt like we saw a lot in one day. Costa Maya felt like it required more planning. Without an excursion, there isn't much beyond the port area. Cozumel was somewhere in the middle. We went to a beach club that was nice but fairly standard. I think the biggest issue was timing. We docked later in one port and it cut into what we could do, which made it feel rushed. Still, the variety between ports made the trip interesting.

name: Linda G.
review: Just got back and Roatan was my favorite. We did the 'Easy Roatan' tour which was perfect for seniors. No crazy hiking, just a nice air-conditioned bus showing us the views and the local culture. Cozumel was way too crowded for me. There were five ships in port and you could barely walk on the sidewalks downtown. We ended up going back to the ship after an hour. Costa Maya was better; the port shopping is great if you like to haggle for souvenirs.

name: Logan Pierce
review: Cozumel was the easiest to explore on our own since taxis were readily available and the town layout was simple to navigate. Roatan was more structured for us, we joined a guided island tour that included viewpoints and a short beach break. Costa Maya was the least engaging because we didn't book an excursion and just stayed within the port zone. It was clean and organized but didn't really feel like we experienced the destination itself. I think this itinerary rewards advance planning more than anything else.

name: TheMillerFamily
review: Costa Maya was a struggle with the kids. The walk from the ship to the taxis is long and there's not much shade. Once we got to the water park it was fine, but getting there was stressful. Cozumel was much easier. We did the glass-bottom boat and it kept the little ones entertained without them having to get in the water. Roatan was the highlight for the teens; they did the zipline and said it was the scariest and coolest thing they've ever done. I liked the chocolate factory there. It's a good itinerary for families but be prepared for a lot of walking in the heat. Make sure to bring plenty of small bills for tips and taxis in Mexico, as they aren't great about making change for twenty-dollar bills. Roatan accepted US dollars everywhere we went.

name: Daniela Rossi
review: Each port had its pros and cons, but the biggest factor for me was how time was managed. In Roatan, we booked a nature-focused excursion that included a guided walk through a forested area and a short beach stop. It was memorable, but we were constantly aware of the clock, which made it hard to fully relax. Costa Maya required a longer commitment; we chose to visit nearby ruins, which meant an early departure and a fairly long bus ride. The site itself was impressive, but I would have preferred either more time there or a shorter travel distance. Cozumel felt like a reset-we intentionally avoided excursions and just explored at our own pace. That ended up being the most relaxing day. If anything, I'd say this itinerary works best if you mix structured excursions with at least one completely open day.

name: Elena Petrova
review: From a logistics perspective, each port required a different strategy. Roatan excursions felt slightly rushed, especially with transportation delays getting back. Costa Maya involved committing to longer travel times if you wanted to see anything beyond the port, which we did by visiting ruins. The site itself was impressive but I wish we had more time there. Cozumel was the easiest to manage. We skipped excursions and just explored at our own pace, which ended up being the most relaxing day of the trip. I think the itinerary works best if you balance structured activities with at least one flexible day.

name: H_Yamamoto
review: For those visiting Roatan, the monkeys are very clever, so watch your pockets! We had a wonderful day at the Gumbalimba Park. It was very well organized. In Cozumel, we participated in a turtle salvage program which was very educational. It was moving to see the conservation efforts. Costa Maya was our last stop. We found the port area to be very loud with music, which made it hard to relax. We walked further out to find a quiet spot on the beach. The sand is very white and beautiful, but there is a lot of coral rubble, so water shoes are a good idea. Overall, a good variety of islands, though the time spent in each felt a little rushed due to the ship's schedule. I would have liked to stay in Cozumel until sunset.

name: Sophie Nguyen
review: We did a short island tour in Roatan that included scenic stops and it felt more personal than expected. Costa Maya was very commercial and we didn't feel motivated to leave the port area. Cozumel had more energy, but the crowds made it harder to enjoy walking around. I wish Costa Maya had more accessible independent options.

name: D_Chen88
review: Cozumel was 100% the highlight for my husband and me. We did the clear kayak excursion and seeing the fish right through the bottom of the boat was surreal. For Costa Maya, we actually stayed on the ship. We've been there before and the port area is just too touristy for our liking. It was nice to have the pool to ourselves while everyone else was fighting for space at the beach clubs. In Roatan, we visited the Maya Key private island. It was a very short boat ride from the pier and had great snorkeling right off the dock. It was a nice mix of relaxation and activity. The timing at each port felt sufficient, though Cozumel always feels like it needs a full two days to really explore. Highly recommend the kayak tour if you want something unique!

name: Anika Shah
review: We chose a cultural tour in Roatan that included small towns and scenic stops, which gave a better sense of the island beyond the port. Costa Maya was more relaxed for us; we didn't book anything and spent time walking around the port shops and pool area. In Cozumel, we joined a short guided walking tour that covered local streets and a small market area, which was interesting but very hot and crowded. I think Roatan had the most balanced experience between activity and scenery, while Costa Maya was more passive unless you plan something specific.

name: Bruno Almeida
review: Roatan was the only stop where we felt like we actually experienced the island beyond the cruise infrastructure. We joined a small island drive and stopped at a viewpoint that overlooked the coast. Costa Maya was very organized but felt contained, almost like everything was built around cruise passengers. We didn't venture far. Cozumel was the most active day for us since we walked around town and visited a couple of local shops and cafes. It was easy to move around but also quite crowded with other cruise guests. The itinerary overall was fine, but Roatan clearly had the most memorable off-ship experience.

name: Fatima Zahra
review: Roatan felt the most unique out of the three ports. We did a small group tour that included a cultural stop and a beach break, and it didn't feel overly commercial. Costa Maya was a bit overwhelming when you first get off the ship, lots of vendors and noise. Cozumel was more relaxed and easy to figure out.

name: Derrick Johnson
review: I've cruised a few times and Roatan felt the most authentic of the three stops. We hired a driver for the day and visited local neighborhoods before heading to a snorkeling spot. The reef was impressive, probably the best water visibility of the trip. Costa Maya was my least favorite. The port area is basically a shopping complex, and the beach clubs all felt similar. We picked one randomly and it was fine but nothing special. Cozumel had more flexibility-we rented a scooter and drove along the coast, stopping wherever looked interesting. That freedom made a big difference. If I did this itinerary again, I'd plan something more structured for Costa Maya and keep Roatan and Cozumel more open-ended.

name: Tyler M.
review: I'm a solo traveler and I found Roatan very easy to navigate. I just walked off and found a local driver who took me to West End for $20. Spent the day at a small cafe on the water and did some great shore snorkeling. Cozumel was a bit much for me alone-everyone is trying to pull you into their shop or bar. I ended up going back to the ship after an hour. Costa Maya was actually quite chill if you stay at the very end of the beach away from the cruise pier. The food at the local stalls in Mahahual was much better and cheaper than the port food. I think the time in each port was adequate, though Cozumel feels like it needs a full 12 hours if you want to do the mainland excursions to Tulum.
